tytul: Chive oil for the refrigerator, eaten by the next day (UGA method)
wstep: This card uses the UGA Extension method for oil with non-acidified fresh herbs, here chives: the oil is heated to 180 °F (82 °C) before the herbs are added, and the oil is kept in the refrigerator or frozen. UGA allows at most 4 days in the refrigerator, and NCHFP gives no more than 4 days for garlic in oil. This card uses the shorter limit of the German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR): eat the oil no later than the day after you make it.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Home-made oils with non-acidified garlic or herbs must never be stored at room temperature.
For garlic in oil, NCHFP says to make it fresh and keep it in the refrigerator at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or lower for no more than 4 days.

akapity: Vegetables and herbs in oil meet the conditions for botulinum toxin production: spores can be present, oil keeps oxygen out, and the pH is above 4.6.
You cannot tell from the look, smell or taste of the oil whether botulism is a risk.
It covers fresh chives added to heated oil; the acidification method was developed only for garlic, basil, oregano and rosemary and must not be used for chives.
Using dried chives instead does not ensure a safe oil: without a laboratory measurement you cannot know whether dried herbs are dry enough.
Make only as much oil as you will eat by the day after you make it.
Wash the glass container thoroughly and boil it for 10 minutes.
Choose good-quality chives, wash them thoroughly and pat them dry.
Heat the oil to 180 °F (82 °C), checking it with a kitchen thermometer, and only then add the chives.
Put the oil with the chives into the sterilized container, close it and keep it in the refrigerator.
Keep the oil in the refrigerator at 40 °F (4 °C) or lower.
Eat the oil no later than the day after you made it, and throw away what is left.
The BfR advises against making herb oils in advance and storing them at home.
Alternatively, freeze the oil until you are ready to use it.
